newsitem.title: USA: Gateway surges on bullish Wall St view.
newsitem.headline: Gateway surges on bullish Wall St view.

text.p: Shares of Gateway 2000 Inc, which sells PCs directly to customers, soared on a bevvy of positive news, including its stock's move to the NYSE and aggressive comments from its CEO at its annual meeting.
Earlier Wednesday, Gateway announced a two-for-one stock split, a share repurchase plan of up to 10 million shares, post-split and that its shares will move to the NYSE May 22.
Analysts also said aggressive comments by CEO Ted Waitt were fueling a bullish view on Wall Street on the North Sioux City, S.D. firm, which sells PCs in boxes with a cow motif.
Gateway shares were up 7-5/8 to 69 in heavy trading.

"They said they are going to be more aggressive in the year ahead, in particular in the corporate market," said Daniel Ries, a Nomura Research analyst. In 1996, business customers made up about one half of sales, Gateway said.

Rival Dell Computer Corp, the Austin, Texas based company that pioneered the direct model when founder Michael Dell started selling PCs out of his college dorm room, has an even bigger percentage of corporate customers.
"Gateway realizes that the value is in the corporate space," Ries said. More emphasis on big corporate sales means more predictable orders and not so much seasonal business.
"That is one emphasis we have this year is in the corporate marketplace," said Rick Snyder, Gateway's president and chief operating officer, in a phone interview.

"We will be enhancing our product offerings and we are adding account people," Synder said, but he did not have any numbers of how many phone reps and field sales people Gateway will be adding to emphasize large corporate accounts.

He said Gateway remains on track with its previous projections of growing at about twice the pace of the PC industry, which is estimated to grow at about 15 percent this year, worldwide, in terms of unit shipments.
